question: Which of the following parts of the engine is used to compress the charge during compression stroke and to transmit the gas force to the connecting rod and then to the crankshaft during power stroke?
solution:
The correct answer is __Piston.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Piston__ is a crucial component of an internal combustion engine.
 
• During the compression stroke, the piston compresses the air-fuel mixture (charge) within the cylinder.
 
• During the power stroke, the combustion of the compressed charge generates gas force, which is transmitted by the piston to the connecting rod.
 
• The connecting rod further transfers this force to the crankshaft, converting linear motion into rotational motion.
 
• Pistons are usually made of lightweight and durable materials like aluminum alloys.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Cylinder Head:**

 
 
• The cylinder head is located at the top of the cylinder and houses components like valves and spark plugs.
 
• It seals the cylinder to contain the combustion process and allows the entry/exit of air-fuel mixture and exhaust gases.
 
 
 
• **Cylinder Block:**
 
 
• The cylinder block is the foundation of the engine, containing cylinders, coolant passages, and oil passages.
 
• It provides structural support and houses the pistons, crankshaft, and connecting rods.
 
 
 
• **Crankcase:**
 
 
• The crankcase encloses and supports the crankshaft, providing a protective housing.
 
• It also acts as a reservoir for engine oil used for lubrication.
